candidates.title: Map variable invoice rows for review

demandEvidence.chore: Map a variable-length CRM array into multiple invoice rows in an external system request.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I cannot map array data for dynamic amount of invoice rows to the HTTP POST module’s “invoice rows” section.

experimentPlan.output: A reviewable draft list of invoice rows mapped from fictional CRM line items, with source values and unresolved fields flagged.
inputs: Fictional CRM record with a variable-length list of line items
Fictional invoice endpoint field guide supplied by the operator
Expected row count and a manually prepared example output
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator supplies one fictional CRM record and asks for a draft payload.
steps: Read the fictional line-item array and the operator supplied field guide.
Map each selected array value into a proposed invoice-row field.
Show the indexed source value beside each drafted row.
Flag missing or ambiguous fields without filling them in.
Ask a person to compare the draft row count and values with the input before any external use.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: On operator supplied fictional records, confirm that every selected input line appears once in the draft, source values match exactly, and ambiguous mappings are flagged.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A person supplies and verifies the endpoint field guide, checks every row, and authorizes any real request. The experiment does not send HTTP requests, persist invoices, or determine tax treatment.
unverified: Whether the target endpoint accepts this payload structure
Whether Make mapping handles the customer actual variable arrays as proposed
Invoice persistence, tax correctness, authentication, and live execution

ease.reason: A beginner can test fictional arrays; Make documentation shows indexed array mapping, but not the complete invoice request.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small service firms preparing invoices might pay for row preparation; this single question shows no buyer or payment evidence.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can draft and compare rows; API execution, persistence, and tax behavior remain outside the supported scope.

autonomy.reason: Array values can be mapped in a proposed draft, but no source supports automatic HTTP execution and a person must approve each row.

evidence.reason: The post states a variable invoice-row mapping problem and supplies array examples; the Make guide documents indexed array mapping only.

candidates.reason: Concrete mapping task assessed as a synthetic draft experiment. Provisional mean 5.0 is below the 6 threshold; the supplied Make guide supports indexed array mapping, not HTTP execution, invoice persistence, or tax correctness.

candidates.title: Draft compact email thread summaries

demandEvidence.chore: Create a compact summary of a long email conversation that preserves relevant context for drafting a response.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I use it to create draft prefill with the good knowledge + compact history of the conversation with each mail resume

experimentPlan.output: A compact draft summary of one fictional email thread that lists the latest question, relevant prior context, and unresolved details for a person to check.
inputs: Fictional email thread with sender names removed
A manually written expected summary for comparison
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator provides a fictional multi-message thread for a summary draft.
steps: Read the supplied fictional messages in order.
Identify the latest question and the earlier context needed to understand it.
Draft a short summary and mark uncertain references.
Compare the draft with the operator supplied expected summary.
Have a person correct the summary before using it in any reply.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: For each fictional thread, check that the latest question and required prior context appear, no new facts were added, and uncertain references are visibly marked.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A person supplies synthetic or authorized test messages, checks names and context, and approves any reply. No real mail account access or sending is included.
unverified: No supplied building reference documents email ingestion or summarization
Whether summaries remain accurate across varied thread formats
Any access controls, retention rules, or live email integration

ease.reason: A student can compare fictional thread summaries against a manual reference, but no implementation source is supplied.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: consultants handling long client threads may value summaries; this post establishes no buyer intent or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week test can draft summaries from supplied fictional threads, while varied thread formats and accuracy remain untested.

autonomy.reason: A draft can repeat for supplied threads, but a person must verify context and approve any reply; no email integration is documented.

evidence.reason: The retained post describes compacting long email histories to prefill a draft, but gives no corroborating demand or implementation reference.

candidates.reason: Fresh retained post spans support a bounded fictional-thread summary experiment. Provisional mean 4.8 is below threshold; no supplied implementation reference documents email ingestion or summarization.

rejected.title: FreeApply local job application MCP
rejected.reason: The attached excerpt describes a maker’s local MCP product and privacy design, not a concrete customer chore or request. It does not support demand for a bounded professional-services experiment.

rejected.title: Restore deleted n8n Cloud workflows
rejected.reason: The retained spans describe one accidental deletion that took a customer chatbot offline and expose operational identifiers. This is a single incident/restore case, not a repeated bounded chore suitable for an autonomous service; the spans do not document a safe restoration procedure.

rejected.title: Manage startup operations
rejected.reason: The excerpt only says an operations service will manage startup operations. It identifies no specific existing chore, so scoring a scoped experiment would require inventing duties.

rejected.title: Make ATS access easier
rejected.reason: The excerpt complains that some hiring tools require sales contact, but specifies no concrete task or requested workflow. A software service and chore cannot be scoped from this fragment.

rejected.title: Scale an AWS startup affordably
rejected.reason: The excerpt offers help to bootstrapped startups but names no concrete scaling task or supplied cost data. A specific analysis workflow would be invented from this broad offer.

steps.message: Assessed all seven assigned discussion identities. Two concrete chores received scoped provisional assessments and both remained below the 6 threshold; five assignments lacked a repeatable specific chore or described a one-off incident. No post proposed.
